solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: We hear parental guidance for a wild boxer to be very scary!

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they are spoken, not spelt

parts.words: parental guidance for a wild boxer
parts.note: parental guidance is raising, and the wild boxer is a hare, which famously boxes in spring, so the phrase is hare raising

explanation.surface: A wild boxer's upbringing sounds like a frightening affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Hares stand up and box each other in spring, hence 'wild boxer'. Rearing one is hare raising, which is said exactly like the hyphenated adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so frightening it makes your hair stand on end is terrifying, very scary.

clue.text: Collection of poetry remains sharp — or idle rubbish?

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: rubbish describes the words as a mess, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a poetry anthology is sharp or idle rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' reads as the speaker's verdict on the poems, but it is the signal to rearrange the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman's famous 1896 cycle of poems bears this title, so it is a named collection of poetry.

clue.text: Unit of land area opening up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a door is an opening into a room

explanation.surface: A plot of land is being opened up for development.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is an old English measure of land, a quarter of an acre.

clue.text: Dislike making a reading

parts.note: a reading is one interpretation, a version, as in a reading of a text

explanation.surface: Someone takes against giving a reading in public.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong distaste for something, a dislike.

clue.text: Gull in vacuum cleaner?

definitions.meaning: as a noun, a gull is a dupe, someone easily fooled
playfully, a vacuum cleaner is a machine that draws things up by suction

explanation.surface: A seagull has got trapped inside the vacuum cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe is a gullible person, and a machine that draws in by suction can jokingly be called one too.

clue.text: Feature — part of face so neatly turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie inside the words face so neatly

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A neat upturned nose is part of a pretty face.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Feature — part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the indicator for the hidden letters; 'Feature' alone defines. 'turned up' reverses ESON from faCE SO Neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial features include eyes, mouth and nose, so this is an example of a feature.

clue.text: Rare copy — issu?

parts.note: the word issue, an edition, has been limited by losing its last letter, so this shortened form is what the two words instruct

explanation.surface: A collector's rare copy of a magazine issue, oddly misspelt.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: take an edition (ISSUE) and limit it by cutting its tail, leaving ISSU.
explanation.definitionFit: A small print run makes each copy scarce, so it is a rare copy.

clue.text: Chairman and son in conflict, one seemingly from another era?

indicators.note: words in conflict are in disarray, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A chairman and his son clash, the father looking out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' rearranges CHAIRMAN and SON; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything out of its proper time, like a wristwatch in a Roman epic, is an anachronism.

clue.text: A let-down in schoolboy humour?

parts.note: a let-down is a disappointment, but here it is a cushion letting down its air with a rude noise, a staple schoolboy prank

explanation.surface: A disappointment in the world of juvenile jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let-down' suggests disappointment; literally it is something deflating when sat on.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubber prank cushion deflates with a flatulent noise, the classic childish practical joke.

clue.text: Press gathering American material on one children's book

indicators.note: gathering means the first piece collects the others inside it

parts.note: to jam is to press or wedge in
twill is a woven fabric
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The press is collecting American material for a children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places TWILL before I in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmal Crompton's 1922 collection of stories about the scruffy schoolboy William Brown is a children's book.

clue.text: All must conclude, menu found to contain noodles

indicators.note: all must conclude says the final letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees the menu must include noodles.
explanation.definitionFit: Udon are thick Japanese wheat noodles.

clue.text: Land in water has a tenant

definitions.meaning: a small island, a patch of land surrounded by water
a property that has a tenant ..., so the phrase splits as ...

explanation.surface: A little island property has been rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a piece of land in water; split in two, the word says a property is rented.

clue.text: Plate to identify, half missing

indicators.note: half missing means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: to discover something is to identify or find it

explanation.surface: A number plate that can't be identified with half of it missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat round plate is a disc, as in a dinner plate or a vertebral disc.

clue.text: Lift splendid drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, lift means the word is raised, read upwards and so backwards

parts.note: regal means splendid, fit for a king

explanation.surface: A splendid drink gives a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reverses REGAL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink.

clue.text: Bloom has life during hours of sunlight

indicators.note: during says the second piece sits inside the time span named

parts.note: day is the time of light, as opposed to night
is in the sense exists or lives, as in I think therefore I am

explanation.surface: A flower thrives in the daylight hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The daisy is a common flower, a bloom.

clue.text: Start to finish in race proving difficult for one with a will

indicators.note: letters proving difficult are awkward, so they are worked into a new order
finish in picks the last letter of the word race

explanation.surface: From start to finish the race proves hard for a determined runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to finish' reads as a whole race; really START and TO join E, the finish of 'race', and 'proving difficult' scrambles them.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who has made a legal will.

clue.text: Calling nurse, ringing phone at last

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a carer is someone who nurses another

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of phone

explanation.surface: A nurse summoned when the phone finally rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation, one's chosen profession or line of work.

clue.text: Bug in flower coming up under table

indicators.note: under places the reversed river below the table in the down entry

parts.note: a table is a list of data

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An insect sits in a flower beneath a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river (it flows), here the Aire, a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is a bacterium causing food poisoning, and a germ is colloquially a bug.

clue.text: Flowers — one comes up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to rise is to come up

explanation.surface: Flowers poke up one by one in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are tall flowering plants, a kind of flower.

clue.text: Extraordinary brain seen in it, pickled

indicators.note: pickled suggests the words are muddled, as if drunk, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A remarkable brain is on display, preserved in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the physicist's brain really was preserved after his death.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's name is used for any genius, so it means an extraordinary brain.

clue.text: Yellow line in capital, first of limos getting clamped by old witch

indicators.note: getting clamped by means the letter is held inside the outer word

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned men into swine

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of limos

explanation.surface: Limousines on a yellow line in the capital get wheel-clamped.
explanation.walkthrough: The yellow line suggests parking rules, but it is a Tube line: the Circle line is yellow on the London Underground map.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Circle line is shown in yellow on the Underground map, a line in the capital.

clue.text: Dance spins bringing lascivious look

indicators.note: spins means the word turns round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A dancer's spins draw a lecherous glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, lustful look, a lascivious look.

clue.text: Police corruption

definitions.meaning: British slang for the police, especially detectives

explanation.surface: A story of police corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: British criminal slang for the police, and dirt or obscenity.

clue.text: Beer ticket returned

indicators.note: returned means the word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: a slip is a small piece of paper such as a ticket

explanation.surface: A beer is bought with a ticket handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager beer.

clue.text: Talk about no-win situation for Asian national!

indicators.note: talk about says the word is judged by its spoken form

parts.note: a tie is a draw in which nobody wins

explanation.surface: An Asian person discusses a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a native of Thailand, a Southeast Asian national.

clue.text: Polish-American writer entering drama school

indicators.note: entering says the letters are found inside the words drama school

explanation.surface: An émigré author enrolls at a drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: Sholem Asch was a Polish-born American novelist and playwright writing in Yiddish.

clue.text: Puzzle setter built this arch across island in stone

indicators.note: in places everything that follows inside the stone

parts.note: agate is an ornamental stone

indicators.note: across means the scrambled letters span the island letter
built means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone built an arch of stone spanning an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle setter' tempts toward a crossword compiler; it is the crime writer, whose mysteries are puzzles. 'built', 'across' and 'in' are the three signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime novelist set her readers whodunnit mysteries to solve, so she is a setter of puzzles.

clue.text: Orbiting Mars initially, I came in the new Tardis, perhaps?

indicators.note: orbiting means circling, so the scrambled letters go round the Mars letter
new says the words are made afresh in another order
initially picks the first letter of Mars

explanation.surface: A traveller lands on Mars in the new Tardis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbiting' looks like spaceflight scenery but tells the scrambled letters to circle the initial of Mars; 'new' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who's police box travels through time, an example of the device, hence the question mark.
